justifications.label: Touch back-propagation (depth-1) shows paradigm flow from mobile to desktop; mobile dominance acceleration (depth-2) shows the market force driving it — together they reveal that mobile didn't just win the platform war but erased the loser's identity

mobile-back-propagation-undermines-fitts.text: Mobile's back-propagation to desktop undermines Fitts's law at its original source: the very platform where Fitts-validated mouse interaction was the foundational model (Card/English/Burr → mouse → Mac → GUI standard) now adopts touch-derived patterns (natural scrolling, passive scrollbars, gesture navigation) that operate on fundamentally different motor assumptions — erasing the paradigm distinction that Fitts's law helped establish.

justifications.label: The desktop platform, whose identity was established through Fitts-validated mouse interaction, now absorbs touch paradigms that operate outside the Fitts model — the law's greatest success becomes its site of obsolescence.

mobile-dominance-accelerated-passive-int.text: The mobile web's rise to dominant platform status coincided with and reinforced the 50-year shift from interactive to passive scroll controls — touch interfaces removed the need for visible scrollbar affordances, collapsing them to output-only indicators and validating the trajectory from Bravo (1974) through iPhone (2007).

justifications.label: Mobile platform dominance (depth-1) and scrollbar passivization (depth-1) converged in the touch paradigm shift

mobile-erodes-platform-interaction-diver.text: Mobile back-propagation appears to be narrowing aspects of the historically evolved macOS/Windows interaction divergence (control placement conventions, modality semantics, platform terminology) by introducing shared mobile-derived conventions such as inertial scrolling and passive controls. While this trend moves both platforms toward greater convergence in certain interaction dimensions, the extent to which it dissolves platform-specific design identity — as opposed to layering mobile conventions atop persistent native differences — remains a matter of degree rather than a settled conclusion.

justifications.label: the documented platform divergence (spatial layout, modal behavior, naming) is being actively eroded by the documented back-propagation of mobile paradigms to desktop — specific divergences become candidates for convergence

mobile-first-vs-graceful-degradation.text: Mobile-first design uses progressive enhancement (build for smallest screen first, then enhance upward); graceful degradation is the opposite (build for desktop first, then adapt down).

mobile-invalidated-complete-human-perfor.text: Mobile dominance has challenged both halves of the human-performance model that guided decades of desktop GUI design: the cognitive half (progressive disclosure becomes mandatory under the double squeeze of small viewport and ~7±2 working-memory limit) and the motor half (Fitts's law, while still applicable, describes a fundamentally different interaction mode on touch surfaces where precise pointer targeting gives way to gesture-based scrolling, with no infinite-target screen edges).

justifications.label: mobile simultaneously disrupted the cognitive and motor models that jointly constituted the desktop-era human performance envelope

mobile-surpassed-desktop-traffic-2014-20.text: Mobile devices surpassed desktop for global web traffic around 2014-2015; as of April 2015, mobile accounted for 63.3% of all global web traffic.

mobile-surpassed-desktop-traffic-late-20.text: Mobile web traffic surpassed desktop traffic in late 2016; as of 2025 mobile is approximately 62% and desktop approximately 36%.

mobile-touch-disrupted-fitts-law-paradig.text: The quantitative HCI models (Fitts's law) that helped validate the mouse and catalyze the GUI revolution originated in a precise-pointer-targeting paradigm, yet the mobile touch era — which reduced reliance on such targeting in favor of gesture-based scrolling — coincided with and reinforced the same 50-year trend from interactive to passive controls that those models had earlier shaped.

justifications.label: Fitts's law built the mouse paradigm, then mobile touch inverted it — the models persisted but the interaction mode they describe transformed

mobile-web-became-dominant-platform.text: Three developments marked the rise of mobile web as a major platform: mobile traffic surpassing desktop in late 2016, Google's mobile-first indexing policy in March 2018 which made responsive design essential for search ranking, and the emergence of the PWA concept coined in 2015 by Berriman and Russell.

justifications.label: Traffic, search ranking, and technical capability all shifted toward mobile within a 3-year window

mobile-web-emerged-across-three-phases.text: Mobile web access emerged across three distinct phases, each originating in a different geographic market: commercial mobile connectivity (Finland, 1996), mobile-specific browsing service (i-mode, Japan, 1999), and mobile-adaptive web design (first responsive site Audi.com, Germany/global, 2001) — suggesting mobile web was a convergent innovation across independent regional efforts rather than a centrally planned platform transition.

justifications.label: Three geographic origins (Finland, Japan, Germany) for three distinct mobile web capabilities suggest convergent evolution driven by shared constraints rather than coordinated development

mobile-web-users-5-34-billion-2025.text: GSMA estimates 5.34 billion mobile web users worldwide as of 2025, approximately 60% of the world population.

mock-objects-vs-ui-mockups.text: In software engineering, mock objects isolate unit tests by simulating dependencies, while UI mockups visualize interfaces without backend logic — two distinct uses of the term 'mock'.

mockup-vs-prototype-distinction.text: A mockup is not always a prototype; it becomes a prototype only when it provides at least partial system functionality and enables testing.

modal-button-placement-windows-macos.text: Platform convention for modal button placement: Windows places the affirmative action button at lower-right; macOS places it as the rightmost command.

modal-confirmation-pattern-doubly-underm.text: The complete modal confirmation pattern — attention capture through modality plus proper button ordering and non-destructive defaults — is independently compromised at both layers: modals fail at reliable attention capture (focus-stealing risk) and confirmation dialogs fail as safety nets (habituation and overuse), leaving no trustworthy modal mechanism for protecting users from destructive actions.

justifications.label: Both component claims are independently OUT (each gated by distinct negative evidence); combining reveals that the full pattern has no functioning layer

modal-dialogs-reliable-attention-capture.text: Modal dialogs reliably capture user attention for critical decisions by disabling parent window interaction.

justifications.label: Modals block parent interaction by design, but focus stealing enables malicious input interception, undermining the safety assumption

modal-focus-stealing-security-risk.text: Focus stealing is a security concern with modal windows: modals can intercept input (keystrokes, mouse clicks) intended for other applications.

modal-habituation-undo-preferred.text: Usability experts recommend undo over warning dialogs for destructive actions because habituation causes users to dismiss warnings without reading them.

modal-opposite-is-modeless.text: The opposite of a modal window is modeless (not 'non-modal'); modeless windows allow concurrent interaction with the parent.

modal-window-blocks-parent.text: A modal window creates a mode where the main window cannot be used until the modal is dismissed.

modal-window-disables-parent-interaction.text: A modal window disables interaction with the parent window while keeping the parent visible — this is its defining characteristic.

modeless-dialogs-preferred-ux.text: Modeless dialogs are generally preferred for good UX because they don't force a mode of operation on the user

modern-web-app-transcends-document-model.text: SPAs (dynamic DOM rewriting, History API navigation) and PWAs (service worker lifecycle, offline capability, install criteria) together transform the browser from a document viewer into an application runtime, breaking the original page-based web model.

justifications.label: SPA and PWA technologies jointly negate the browser's original document assumptions — no page loads, offline operation, installability

modified-delphi-card-sort-iterative-cons.text: Modified-Delphi card sorting is iterative: each participant refines the previous participant's sort, reaching consensus with fewer participants

mosaic-first-mainstream-browser-april-19.text: Mosaic, released in April 1993, was the first mainstream browser and is credited with sparking the 1990s Internet boom.

ms-office-3-introduced-context-menus-199.text: Microsoft Office v3.0 introduced context menus for copy/paste in 1990.

munsell-system-1905-hue-value-chroma.text: The Munsell color system (1905) formalized three color attributes: hue, value (lightness), and chroma (saturation).

namco-galaxian-1979-sprite-scrolling-arc.text: The Namco Galaxian arcade board (1979) pioneered the sprite-over-scrolling-background architecture that became the basis for Nintendo's NES.

nassi-shneiderman-diagram-1973-no-goto.text: The Nassi-Shneiderman diagram (1973), co-developed by Isaac Nassi and Ben Shneiderman, is a graphical model for structured programming that replaces flowcharts and eliminates unrestricted transfers of control (GOTOs).

native-browser-lazy-loading-since-2020.text: Native browser lazy loading (via the HTML loading attribute) has been supported by major browsers since 2020, requiring no JavaScript framework.

nav-bar-navigational-control-category.text: Navigation bars are categorized as 'Navigational' graphical control elements, distinct from 'Containers' like toolbars and menu bars.

nav-tag-contains-unordered-list.text: The standard HTML pattern for a navigation bar is a <nav> element wrapping a <ul> with <li> items containing <a> links.

neumorphism-blends-flat-with-soft-shadow.text: Neumorphism is a post-flat design style that blends flat design with subtle depth cues such as soft shadows and highlights.

newton-white-light-spectrum-1672.text: Newton demonstrated in 1672 that white light is composed of a spectrum of colors and that color arises from reflection/absorption of wavelengths, not as an intrinsic property of objects.

nfb-v-target-2006-ada-web-accessibility.text: NFB v. Target Corp. (2006) set U.S. legal precedent for website accessibility under the Americans with Disabilities Act.

nielsen-10-heuristics-finalized-2005.text: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics were finalized in 2005.

nielsen-10-heuristics-no-research-valida.text: No research-based validation of Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics exists; they were developed for simpler 1990s interfaces.

nielsen-10-usability-heuristics.text: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics are: visibility of system status, match between system and real world, user control and freedom, consistency and standards, error prevention, recognition rather than recall, flexibility and efficiency of use, aesthetic and minimalist design, help users recognize/diagnose/recover from errors, and help and documentation.

nielsen-2006-77pct-no-scroll.text: Jakob Nielsen's 2006 study found that 77% of website visitors do not scroll past the initial viewport.

nielsen-5-user-testing-principle.text: Nielsen's 5-user testing principle states that five test users per usability test session is sufficient to uncover most usability problems, based on Nielsen & Landauer's 1993 mathematical model.

nielsen-dual-evaluation-methodology.text: Nielsen established a complete usability evaluation framework combining two complementary methods: fast expert review (heuristic evaluation, 3-5 independent evaluators) for qualitative insight and efficient empirical testing (5-user principle, ~85% problem discovery) for behavioral validation.

justifications.label: Expert review produces qualitative findings; user testing produces empirical measurements — complementary not redundant

nielsen-five-usability-goals.text: Nielsen's five usability goals (from Usability Engineering, 1993) are: Learnability, Efficiency, Memorability, low Error rate, and Satisfaction.

nielsen-five-users-85-percent.text: Nielsen's model suggests five users per iterative round of usability testing uncover approximately 85% of problems on average, though the actual range varies from 55% to 100%.

nielsen-heuristic-eval-expert-review-not.text: Heuristic evaluation is an expert review method (3-5 UX experts judge a UI against heuristics), not a user testing method.

nielsen-heuristics-validated-evaluation-.text: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics provide a validated framework for expert-based usability evaluation, as evidenced by their status as the most popular inspection method.

justifications.label: Popularity and structured methodology suggest validity, but absence of research-based validation undermines the "validated" claim

nielsen-landauer-problem-discovery-formu.text: The Nielsen/Landauer usability problem discovery formula is U = 1 - (1 - p)^n, where U is the proportion of problems uncovered, p is the probability one participant finds a specific problem, and n is the number of participants.

nielsen-norman-group-cofounded-1998.text: Nielsen Norman Group was co-founded in 1998 by Jakob Nielsen and Donald Norman.

nielsen-norman-group-founded-1998.text: The Nielsen Norman Group was co-founded by Don Norman and Jakob Nielsen in 1998 as a consultancy focused on evidence-based UX.

nielsen-norman-methodology-empirically-c.text: The Nielsen-Norman methodology — theoretical design principles grounded in catastrophic failure investigation plus dual evaluation methodology (expert review + user testing) — constitutes an empirically complete framework for UX practice.

justifications.label: Norman's principles have empirical grounding in failure analysis (depth-1) and Nielsen's dual methodology is structured (depth-1), but the heuristic evaluation component lacks research validation (depth-0), creating a gap in the empirical foundation

nielsen-ten-usability-heuristics.text: Nielsen's 10 Usability Heuristics are: (1) Visibility of system status, (2) Match between system and real world, (3) User control and freedom, (4) Consistency and standards, (5) Error prevention, (6) Recognition rather than recall, (7) Flexibility and efficiency of use, (8) Aesthetic and minimalist design, (9) Help users recognize/diagnose/recover from errors, (10) Help and documentation.

nigel-cross-designerly-ways-of-knowing-1.text: Nigel Cross's 'Designerly Ways of Knowing' (1982) established design thinking as a distinct form of knowledge relevant beyond professional design

nimas-2006-accessible-materials-blind-st.text: NIMAS legislation (effective December 2006) requires U.S. K-12 publishers to provide accessible materials for blind students; TUI is a technology that can satisfy this mandate.

nngroup-84pct-attention-difference-above.text: NNgroup (Amy Schade) found an 84% average difference in user engagement between above-the-fold and below-the-fold content.

no-universal-primary-colors.text: No universal primary colors exist — any set of three primaries produces only a limited gamut, never the full range of human color perception.

norman-attractive-interfaces-work-better.text: Norman (2002) argued that design aesthetics can enhance usability — attractive interfaces tend to work better.

norman-coined-user-centered-design-1986.text: Don Norman introduced the term 'user-centered design' in 1986 in the book 'User Centered System Design' co-edited with Stephen Draper.

norman-failure-investigation-pipeline-co.text: The UX methodology pipeline — from catastrophic failure investigation (Norman/Three Mile Island) through quantitative behavioral laws (Fitts/Hick) to institutionalized practice (NNGroup) — completed its full arc from disaster to profession on the desktop paradigm, only for mobile to invalidate the cognitive assumptions (progressive disclosure for scrolling, Fitts-calibrated pointing) that the pipeline's own success had embedded into standard practice.

justifications.label: the methodology pipeline ran failure→theory→practice→disruption, with its own artifacts creating the disruption conditions

norman-failure-methodology-applicable-to.text: Norman's methodology of deriving design principles from catastrophic failure investigation (Three Mile Island → four design principles) is directly applicable to the web's ethical catastrophe: the confirmation dialog's fractal self-reinforcement pattern demonstrates the same class of systemic HMI failure that TMI represented — cognitive shaping producing outcomes invisible to operators/enforcers — and could yield ethical design principles through the same investigative lens, unless the ethical gap's self-reinforcing inheritance paradox prevents any external methodology from breaking the cycle.

justifications.label: TMI produced durable principles because the failure was bounded; the web's ethical failure may be structurally unbounded due to the inheritance paradox, making the same investigative method insufficient

norman-first-ux-architect-title-apple-19.text: Don Norman was the first person to hold the job title 'User Experience Architect' at Apple in 1993.

norman-four-design-principles.text: Norman's four design principles are: (1) simplify task structure so possible actions are intuitive, (2) make things visible (model, actions, results, feedback), (3) achieve correct mappings between intended results and required actions, (4) embrace and exploit system constraints.

norman-nielsen-complementary-ux-methodol.text: Norman (design principles derived from catastrophic failure investigation) and Nielsen (empirical dual methodology combining expert review with user testing) constitute complementary halves of modern UX practice — theory from failure analysis plus measurement from structured evaluation — formalized through their 1998 NNGroup partnership.

justifications.label: Norman's theoretical contribution (depth-1), his catastrophic-failure empirical basis (depth-1), and Nielsen's evaluation methodology (depth-1) are independently established; combining reveals the complementary structure

norman-principles-informed-by-catastroph.text: Norman's involvement in investigating the Three Mile Island accident — a canonical example of poor human-machine interface design contributing to catastrophic failure — suggests that real-world design failures informed his theoretical framework, including his four design principles around task simplicity, visibility, correct mappings, and constraints.

justifications.label: Norman's investigation of Three Mile Island preceded and informed his formalization of design principles

norman-replaced-ucd-with-hcd-2013.text: Norman replaced 'user-centered design' with 'human-centered design' in the revised 2013 edition of The Design of Everyday Things, acknowledging the importance of aesthetics and emotion.

norman-shallice-model-executive-attentio.text: The Norman-Shallice model is a framework of attentional control of executive functioning that includes the supervisory attentional system, developed by Don Norman and Tim Shallice.

norman-shaped-ux-as-discipline.text: Don Norman is among the most influential figures in establishing UX as a professional discipline — co-introducing the term 'user-centered design' (1986), holding what is described as the first 'User Experience Architect' job title at Apple (1993), refining core vocabulary by distinguishing signifiers from affordances (2013), and co-founding Nielsen Norman Group (1998).

justifications.label: Four distinct firsts/milestones attributed to one person across three decades

norman-signifiers-vs-affordances-2013.text: Norman introduced 'signifiers' in his 2013 revision to distinguish from affordances: affordances determine what actions are possible, while signifiers communicate where and how to act.

norman-three-mile-island-investigation.text: Don Norman was part of the investigation team for the 1979 Three Mile Island nuclear accident, a formative case study in human factors and interface design failures.

nvda-free-jaws-commercial-voiceover-buil.text: NVDA is a free/open-source screen reader; JAWS is the most popular commercial screen reader on Windows; VoiceOver is built into all Apple platforms.

observation-articulation-gap-validates-d.text: Apple's 1982 finding that 95% of usability stumbling blocks were identified through body language observation — because users could not articulate problems — is consistent with the rationale behind Nielsen's methodological split between expert heuristic review and observational user testing: both approaches appear to compensate for an observation-articulation gap, where critical design failures may manifest physically rather than verbally.

justifications.label: Apple's empirical finding independently validates the need for Nielsen's dual evaluation approach by demonstrating that user self-report is insufficient

onboarding-25-percent-us-workers-newcome.text: Up to 25% of US workers are newcomers engaged in the onboarding/organizational socialization process at any given time.

open-card-sort-generative-closed-evaluat.text: Open card sorting is generative (participants create their own category names to discover classification patterns); closed card sorting is evaluative (participants sort into predetermined categories to test effectiveness)

opposite-survival-strategies-create-ethi.text: The web's two most durable design achievements survived through strategies with diametrically opposite ethical implications: accessibility's institutional embedding (W3C → WCAG → ISO → legal compliance) created enforceable ethical obligations, while progressive disclosure's dual invisibility placed it permanently outside any enforcement mechanism — a design achievement's survival strategy determines whether it can contribute to the platform's ethical infrastructure.

justifications.label: Institutional survival enables ethical enforcement; invisible survival precludes it — the survival mechanism itself predetermines ethical contribution

os2-workplace-shell-secondary-button-dra.text: OS/2 Workplace Shell used the secondary (right) mouse button for drag-and-drop, unlike Mac/Windows which use the primary button.

overlapping-frameworks-compensate-indivi.text: The overlap among Nielsen's 10 heuristics, Norman's 4 design principles, and ISO 9241's 7 dialogue principles provides redundant coverage for usability evaluation — gaps in one framework are compensated by the others, and the approach's status as the most popular inspection method validates its practical utility.

justifications.label: framework redundancy and popularity suggest practical value, but if the dominant framework (Nielsen's) lacks empirical validation, the evidential basis of the overlap is weakened rather than strengthened by consensus

overlapping-usability-heuristic-framewor.text: Multiple overlapping heuristic frameworks exist — Nielsen's 10 heuristics, Norman's 4 design principles, ISO 9241's 7 dialogue principles — with substantial conceptual overlap but different organizational structures, creating a fragmented evaluation landscape where practitioners must choose or reconcile frameworks.

justifications.label: Three independent heuristic codifications from different traditions (industry, academic, standards body) cover similar ground without convergence

page-up-down-windows-vs-mac-behavior.text: Page Up/Page Down behavior differs by platform: on Windows it moves the caret by one visible page, on Mac it scrolls without moving the caret.

pagination-replaced-foliation-1550.text: Pagination (numbering every page sequentially) replaced foliation (numbering only front sides of folios) as standard practice around 1550.

pagination-supports-permanent-links-infi.text: Pagination supports permanent links via URL parameters (e.g., offset); infinite scrolling does not support deep linking to specific positions.

paradigm-independent-complexity-manageme.text: The web's two complementary complexity management tools — IA for structural organization (navigation predictability) and progressive disclosure for cognitive load (limiting visible choices within working memory bounds) — operate on paradigm-independent perceptual foundations (Gestalt grouping within Miller's capacity) that should constrain interface exploitation regardless of platform shift, because predictable navigation and bounded choice sets structurally reduce the attack surface for confusion-based and overload-based manipulation.

justifications.label: structural+cognitive complexity management on paradigm-independent foundations should constrain exploitation — but 97% dark pattern prevalence refutes this empirically

parallax-scrolling-first-moon-patrol.text: Parallax scrolling (multiple layers at different scroll rates to simulate depth) was first featured in the arcade game Moon Patrol.

parc-primitive-divergence-instantiates-g.text: The divergent fates of Xerox PARC interaction primitives under mobile selective pressure — scrollbar degraded monotonically from interactive to passive, hamburger icon revived by mobile screen constraints — can be read as instances of the self-undermining mechanism operating at the artifact level: the platform success that PARC primitives enabled may have contributed to the mobile transition that selectively fossilized some primitives while accidentally reviving others, suggesting self-undermining can operate down to individual artifacts.

justifications.label: PARC's specific artifact-level divergence confirms self-undermining operates at every organizational scale including individual interaction primitives

parc-primitives-divergent-under-mobile-s.text: Xerox PARC/Star-era interaction primitives underwent structurally divergent fates under mobile's selective pressure: the scrollbar degraded monotonically from interactive control to passive indicator, while the hamburger icon was resurrected from dormancy by mobile screen constraints — revealing that mobile selects for compact/hidden navigation patterns while degrading continuous-feedback controls, a systematic bias toward reduced-agency interaction.

justifications.label: Two primitives from the same institutional origin responded to the same platform pressure in opposite directions, revealing mobile's structural selection bias

partial-checkpoint-most-common-undo-stra.text: Partial checkpoint (saving only changed state) is the most commonly used reverse strategy for implementing undo in practice.

perceived-performance-distinct-from-real.text: Perceived performance is the user's subjective experience of speed, distinct from real (measurable elapsed time) performance.

performance-graphs-individual-reference-.text: Performance graphs use an individual reference standard (self-comparison over time), fostering mastery orientation, unlike leaderboards which use a social reference standard fostering competitive orientation.

perq-first-commercial-gui-1979.text: The PERQ workstation (1979) by Three Rivers Computer Corporation was the first commercially available GUI computer.

persistence-and-immunity-structurally-de.text: The web's design knowledge persists through three survival mechanisms (structural substrate, platform embedding, cognitive embedding) but its three immunity layers (visual/Swiss Style, enforcement/technical, design-artifact/progressive disclosure) operate in dimensions orthogonal to ethical pathology — persistence and immunity are structurally decoupled, meaning the web can preserve design knowledge indefinitely while remaining constitutively unable to defend against ethical degradation.

justifications.label: three immunity layers failing + three survival timescales succeeding → the web's ability to remember and its ability to defend operate in non-overlapping dimensions

personalization-threatens-sole-functiona.text: Material Design's trajectory from prescriptive uniformity to user-driven personalization (dynamic color, expressive design) is testing whether the web's sole functional immune system — Swiss Style as semiotic attractor channeling visual design toward geometric regularity — can maintain its channeling force under customization pressure; if personalization breaks the visual attractor, the web loses immunity in the only dimension where it currently operates while remaining constitutively defenseless in the ethical dimension where it has never operated.

justifications.label: personalization testing attractor stability + immune system already orthogonal to pathology → the web's sole functional defense may itself be eroding

personas-from-ethnographic-interviews.text: In UCD, personas are synthesized from ethnographic interviews (not invented from assumptions) and capture behavior patterns, goals, skills, attitudes, and environment.

personas-prevent-three-pitfalls.text: User personas prevent three specific design pitfalls: Elastic User (stakeholders redefining 'the user'), self-referential design (designers projecting own mental models), and edge-case focus.

phenakistoscope-1832-first-animation-dev.text: The phenakistoscope (1832, Joseph Plateau, Belgium) introduced the principle of modern animation and preceded the zoetrope (1876), flip book (1868), and praxinoscope (1877).

phi-phenomenon-1912-wertheimer.text: Wertheimer's 1912 publication on the phi phenomenon (perceived motion from alternating stationary lights) marks the formal beginning of Gestalt psychology.

platform-convergence-driven-by-paradigm-.text: The historically evolved platform interaction divergence between macOS and Windows is being narrowed not by deliberate standardization but by the same mobile back-propagation that strands the desktop paradigm's usability standards — the force that makes desktop-era distinctions meaningless is simultaneously erasing the distinctions themselves, producing convergence through obsolescence rather than through design.

justifications.label: Platform convergence and paradigm obsolescence share the mobile driver — the distinctions vanish because the paradigm that differentiated them is displaced

platform-convergence-eliminates-measurem.text: Platform convergence driven by mobile back-propagation (macOS and Windows interaction models eroding under touch-derived influence) is eliminating the comparative baselines on which usability measurement depended: as the platform-specific interaction models that usability standards were calibrated against (macOS top-left controls, Windows bottom-right confirmation, different modal behaviors, different scrolling semantics) converge toward a single mobile-influenced norm, not only the standards themselves but the comparative methodology that produced them loses its foundation.

justifications.label: Mobile-driven platform convergence eliminates the between-platform variation that usability comparison depends on

platform-divergence-in-control-placement.text: macOS and Windows differ in UI control placement conventions: macOS positions window controls top-left (color-coded close/minimize/zoom), while Windows places affirmative modal action buttons at lower-right and macOS places them as the rightmost command — a visible platform-identity difference that may contribute to cross-platform muscle memory differences.

justifications.label: Two placement conventions reveal a consistent left-vs-right platform divergence, not random differences

platform-divergent-interaction-models.text: macOS and Windows diverge across multiple interaction dimensions beyond mere control placement: spatial layout (top-left vs top-right window controls, left-aligned vs right-aligned modal buttons), modal scope (document-modal sheets vs application-modal dialogs), and terminology (pop-up menu vs drop-down list) — requiring deliberate platform-aware decisions for cross-platform products.

justifications.label: extending placement divergence to include modality semantics and terminology reveals systematic platform-level disagreement, not isolated differences

platform-embedding-preserves-design-know.text: Design knowledge can persist through platform embedding even when its originating discipline declines: HCI completed its full industry lifecycle including self-destruction, yet core artifacts it produced — particularly the hyperlink and its accessibility pipeline — survive because they were inherited by the web platform before the discipline's desktop-era foundations were displaced. The web platform thus serves in part as a record of pre-web design traditions, preserved more by platform continuity than by ongoing disciplinary activity.

justifications.label: HCI's self-destruction (depth-6) and the web's pre-web inheritance (depth-5) are the same event viewed from opposite sides — the discipline died, but its artifacts were already embedded in the platform

pli-canonical-pola-violation.text: PL/I's precision conversion rules caused '25 + 1/3' to yield 5.33... instead of the expected 25.33..., making it the canonical POLA violation example.

pola-high-astonishment-redesign-corollar.text: Cowlishaw's 1984 corollary to POLA: if a necessary feature has a high astonishment factor, the correct response is to redesign the feature, not to document the surprise.

pola-origin-pli-bulletin-1967-print-1972.text: The Principle of Least Astonishment (POLA/POLS) was first referenced in the PL/I Bulletin in 1967 and first appeared formally in print in 1972.

postscript-pdf-digital-print-formats.text: PostScript and PDF are the standard file formats for digital print transmission.

pragnanz-overarching-gestalt-law.text: The Law of Prägnanz (good Gestalt) — that people perceive things as regular, orderly, symmetrical, and simple — is the overarching Gestalt principle; all other grouping laws (proximity, similarity, closure, etc.) are refinements of it.

precomputation-improves-perceived-respon.text: Precomputation (performing work ahead of time before user requests it) shifts latency away from user-triggered actions to improve perceived responsiveness.

preserved-knowledge-doubly-compromised-u.text: The web's preserved design knowledge is doubly compromised: it is unvalidatable (measurement apparatus destroyed alongside the measured paradigm) AND the survival mechanisms that preserved it selected for ethical asymmetry (institutional embedding for accessibility vs. cognitive invisibility for progressive disclosure) — the web retains knowledge it cannot verify, through mechanisms that filtered out ethical content.

justifications.label: Unvalidatability and ethically-selective preservation independently degrade the value of surviving design knowledge

preserved-knowledge-unvalidatable-by-des.text: The web preserves design knowledge it can no longer empirically validate: knowledge persists asymmetrically through platform and cognitive embedding (creating survivorship bias favoring technical over ethical knowledge), but the measurement apparatus calibrated to validate that knowledge was destroyed alongside the desktop paradigm it measured — producing preserved knowledge whose current applicability is epistemically indeterminate, persisting by structural inertia rather than confirmed fitness.

justifications.label: Survivorship-biased knowledge preservation plus measurement apparatus destruction means the web retains inherited knowledge but cannot distinguish which of it still applies — preservation without validation

prezi-first-mainstream-zui-2009.text: Prezi, launched in 2009, was the first ZUI to reach mainstream adoption with 50M+ users by 2014.

prinz-achmed-1926-oldest-extant-animated.text: Die Abenteuer des Prinzen Achmed (1926, Lotte Reiniger, Germany) is the oldest extant animated feature film, made using silhouette animation.

progress-indicators-feel-faster-despite-.text: Progress indicators (progress bars, splash screens, spinners) make operations feel faster to users despite consuming a small amount of processing time.

progressive-disclosure-addresses-full-pe.text: Progressive disclosure is a design pattern grounded in the human performance envelope: it reduces Hick's choice set (fewer visible options → faster decisions) and keeps visible items within Miller's ~7±2 working memory capacity. While these two mechanisms are directly supported by the antecedents, the pattern may also shorten Fitts's motor distances (smaller, clustered target space) as a plausible secondary effect, though this link is not explicitly established by the evidence.

justifications.label: the performance envelope identifies three hard constraints; progressive disclosure is the validated pattern that resolves all three at once

progressive-disclosure-as-ethical-recove.text: Progressive disclosure is uniquely positioned to seed ethical design recovery: paradigm-independent (bridges desktop to mobile), protected by the enforcement blind spot from both disruption and co-optation, and demonstrating that cognitive-shaping design can persist without institutional stewardship — the sole surviving artifact with structural leverage in the ethical dimension.

justifications.label: PD has the structural properties (paradigm independence, enforcement invisibility) needed to operate in the ethical dimension, but only if the self-reinforcing gap doesn't block all recovery vectors

progressive-disclosure-bridges-document-.text: Progressive disclosure — the web's sole surviving cognitive design principle — could bridge the document-to-app model transition because its mechanism (defer complexity, reveal on demand) is structurally independent of whether content is document-based or dynamically generated, unlike the accessibility pipeline and standards enforcement which both depend on the document model's semantic structure.

justifications.label: Progressive disclosure's paradigm independence may extend to the document-to-app architectural transition, but the self-reinforcing ethical gap could preclude meaningful adoption

progressive-disclosure-defers-not-remove.text: Progressive disclosure defers advanced or rarely-used features to secondary screens — it does not remove them.

progressive-disclosure-operates-in-enfor.text: The web's sole surviving cognitive design principle (progressive disclosure) operates in the exact dimension — cognitive shaping — that is invisible to quality enforcement; the principle works but no mechanism (Google ranking, Bootstrap adoption, W3C standards) checks whether it is applied.

justifications.label: depth-7; cross-branch — enforcement blindness (invention+cognition vs. technical enforcement) and principle survival (HCI self-undermining vs. paradigm bridge) are independent branches that intersect here

progressive-disclosure-origin-woolsey-19.text: The progressive disclosure concept originates from Kristina Hooper Woolsey's 1985 work at the Apple Human Interface Group.

progressive-disclosure-outlived-parent-d.text: Progressive disclosure appears to be a rare design artifact that outlived the discipline that validated it: it survived HCI's self-undermining cycle largely intact — its simultaneous satisfaction of multiple cognitive constraints (Miller, Hick, Fitts) made it relatively platform-invariant — while UX, the discipline that institutionalized progressive disclosure through ISO standards and professional practice, completed what appears to be a full lifecycle from emergence to displacement within roughly the same generation (~1975–2015). The juxtaposition is notable: an artifact persisting across the paradigm shift that challenged the discipline responsible for formalizing it.

justifications.label: Both parent discipline and its predecessor self-undermined or were displaced; progressive disclosure persisted through both extinctions

progressive-disclosure-persists-through-.text: Progressive disclosure is the web's most durable design pattern because it is doubly invisible: invisible to enforcement mechanisms (cognitive shaping cannot be algorithmically detected or mandated by search ranking) AND operating at a paradigm-independent perceptual level (Gestalt grouping within Miller's bounds works identically on desktop and mobile) — making it simultaneously ungovernable and unkillable.

justifications.label: Enforcement invisibility (depth-7) and paradigm-independent perception (depth-5) are independent survival mechanisms; their intersection explains why progressive disclosure alone survived both the discipline collapse and the platform transition

progressive-disclosure-survived-hci-self.text: Progressive disclosure is a design pattern that appears to have weathered HCI's self-undermining cycle better than most desktop-era constructs — while the theory-to-artifact loop created the desktop paradigm whose mobile successor invalidated many of the original human-performance models, progressive disclosure's grounding in multiple cognitive constraints (Miller, Hick, and plausibly Fitts) gives it a well-supported claim to platform-invariance, making it a credible bridge across the desktop-to-mobile transition that disrupted much of the rest of the performance model.

justifications.label: depth-5 HCI self-undermining + depth-4 paradigm bridge yield the only pattern that transcends the cycle

progressive-disclosure-survives-on-parad.text: Progressive disclosure bridges paradigms (desktop → mobile) because its perceptual foundation — Gestalt grouping operating within Miller's working-memory bound — is paradigm-independent: the grouping mechanism works identically regardless of whether disclosure is triggered by click or swipe.

justifications.label: depth-5; explains WHY progressive disclosure survived the paradigm shift — its foundations are below the paradigm boundary

progressive-disclosure-two-goals.text: Progressive disclosure serves two goals: easier learning (reduces cognitive load and learning curve) and fewer errors (avoids overwhelming users with all options).

progressive-disclosure-universal-paradig.text: Progressive disclosure is a design pattern that addresses both the theoretical human-performance envelope (Miller's memory capacity, Hick's decision time, and plausibly Fitts's motor distances) and the practical mobile-cognitive double-squeeze, making it a well-grounded bridge between desktop and mobile design paradigms.

justifications.label: Progressive disclosure survives the desktop→mobile transition because it addresses the constants (cognitive limits) rather than the variables (input modality, viewport size)

progressive-disclosure-validated-complex.text: Progressive disclosure is a validated complexity management technique: deferring (not removing) advanced features to reduce both cognitive load and error rate, with the macOS print dialog as a canonical and enduring implementation.

justifications.label: Dual goals (easier learning, fewer errors) plus a long-lived real-world example establish practical validity

progressive-enhancement-enforceable-disc.text: The web's two "progressive" strategies occupy opposite sides of the enforcement boundary: progressive enhancement (HTML→CSS→JS layering) operates in the technical dimension and is enforceable through standards compliance and graceful degradation testing, while progressive disclosure (defer advanced features) operates in the cognitive dimension invisible to enforcement — the same pair that covers complementary design dimensions also straddles the fundamental enforcement divide.

justifications.label: Complementary progressive strategies split across the enforcement boundary — technical layering is detectable, cognitive deferral is not

progressive-enhancement-order-html-css-j.text: Progressive enhancement layers content delivery as HTML first (content), then CSS (styling), then JavaScript (interactivity).

progressive-strategies-dual-dimension-co.text: Progressive enhancement (HTML → CSS → JS layering) and progressive disclosure (show essentials, defer advanced features) are complementary "progressive" strategies operating on orthogonal dimensions — enhancement manages technical delivery robustness (graceful degradation when capabilities are missing), disclosure manages cognitive load (graceful degradation when user expertise is limited) — together enabling interfaces that degrade gracefully on both axes simultaneously.

justifications.label: Two independently developed "progressive" strategies cover different failure modes — technical absence and cognitive overload — and compose without interference because they operate on orthogonal dimensions

proportional-thumb-18-year-platform-adop.text: The proportional scrollbar thumb — where thumb size reflects the ratio of visible content to total document length — took 18 years from invention (Smalltalk, 1977) through modern refinement essentially identical to contemporary behavior (GEM, 1985) to adoption by the dominant platform (Windows 95, which previously lacked proportional thumbs despite the concept existing for nearly two decades), demonstrating that even unambiguously superior interaction mechanisms face extended adoption lags when platform incumbents lack competitive pressure to adopt.

justifications.label: Three data points trace an 18-year adoption lag for a single unambiguous interaction improvement

proto-personas-vs-true-personas.text: Proto-personas capture a team's assumptions about users (generative tool); true personas are rooted in research data (evaluative tool) — they are not interchangeable.

prototype-based-programming-cloning.text: In prototype-based programming (e.g., JavaScript), new objects are created by cloning existing prototype objects, which is distinct from class-based OOP.

prototype-six-types.text: The six prototype types are: proof-of-principle (partial functionality), working (all/nearly all functionality), visual/form study (appearance only), user experience (enough for user testing), functional (both function and appearance), and paper (low-fidelity hand-drawn for software UI).

prototype-vs-production-three-difference.text: Prototypes differ from final products in three dimensions: material (may use substitutes), process (alternative fabrication vs mass production), and verification (individual inspection vs statistical QA).

pupillary-response-physiological-measure.text: Task-invoked pupillary response (pupil dilation) is a reliable physiological measure of cognitive load; other physiological measures include heart rate, blood pressure, and respiratory rate

pwa-app-store-support.text: Google Play, Microsoft Store, and Samsung Galaxy Store support PWAs; Apple App Store does not.

pwa-manifest-required-properties.text: A PWA web app manifest (manifest.json) requires name or short_name, start_url, display (standalone/fullscreen/minimal-ui), and icons (192px and 512px versions).

pwa-one-service-worker-per-domain.text: Only one service worker can be active per domain at a time.

pwa-service-worker-cache-vs-http-cache.text: Service worker caches differ from HTTP caches in that they can prefetch content before first use and explicitly discard content when no longer needed.

pwa-service-worker-lifecycle-three-phase.text: The service worker lifecycle has three phases: Registration (browser told SW location), Installation (when no SW exists or update available), and Activation (when all PWA pages are closed).

pwa-term-coined-2015-berriman-russell.text: The term 'progressive web apps' was coined in 2015 by Frances Berriman and Google Chrome engineer Alex Russell.

pwa-three-install-criteria.text: PWA installation requires three technical criteria: served over HTTPS with no active mixed content, a registered service worker with a fetch handler, and a valid web app manifest.

quality-control-uninheritability-time-in.text: The web's inability to acquire quality control is time-invariant: at the historical scale, inheritance transferred quality without control mechanisms from pre-web traditions (HCI's theory-to-artifact loop, Swiss Style's grid substrate); at the intervention scale, external forces can inject knowledge without governance mechanisms — the same structural asymmetry (quality persists, control does not) manifests identically whether the source is a dying discipline or an active intervention, revealing a constitutional property rather than a historical accident.

justifications.label: Inheritance pattern and intervention pattern are the same structural phenomenon at different temporal scales

quantitative-hci-models-shaped-hardware-.text: Fitts's and Hick's laws didn't merely describe interaction post-hoc — Fitts-based evaluation directly validated the mouse over competing input devices (1978), which drove the hardware choice that made the GUI revolution possible (Macintosh 1984), demonstrating that quantitative cognitive models can be causal forces in technology adoption.

justifications.label: The dual-model decomposition of interaction time (depth-1) and Fitts's causal role in mouse adoption (depth-1) together reveal quantitative psychology as a technology-selection mechanism

radio-button-linguistic-skeuomorph-outla.text: The radio button's name — derived from physical car radio preset buttons whose mechanical interlocking enforced mutual exclusivity — is a linguistic skeuomorph that survived the entire visual design language evolution (skeuomorphism → flat → material) that systematically eliminated visual skeuomorphs, demonstrating that naming conventions embed in cognitive-linguistic infrastructure more deeply than visual metaphors embed in perceptual infrastructure: you can redesign what a control looks like but not what a control is called.

justifications.label: Linguistic skeuomorphism persists through the very visual design transitions that eliminated visual skeuomorphism

radio-button-mutual-exclusivity.text: Radio buttons enforce mutually exclusive selection within a group; selecting one automatically deselects any previously selected option in the same group.

radio-button-name-from-car-radios.text: The name 'radio button' originates from physical car radio preset buttons, where pressing one button mechanically pops out the others.

radio-buttons-single-checkboxes-multiple.text: Radio buttons allow only one selection within a group; checkboxes allow multiple independent selections.

radio-vs-checkbox-selection-rule.text: Radio buttons are used when the user must choose exactly one option; checkboxes are used when zero or more selections are valid.

remediation-triply-foreclosed.text: The web's ethical gap is triply foreclosed against remediation: quality control was never inherited and cannot be acquired (time-invariant uninheritability), external intervention cannot perceive the gap it targets (blindness to unmeasurable acceleration), and any intervention that overcame both barriers would reproduce the self-undermining dynamic that created the gap (isomorphic self-defeat) — three independent impossibility results converging on the same conclusion from different causal paths.

justifications.label: Three independently derived depth-22 impossibility results converge on triple foreclosure of remediation

remote-testing-sync-vs-async.text: Remote usability testing is either synchronous (moderated, real-time via video/screen sharing) or asynchronous (unmoderated, auto-logged); asynchronous allows larger sample sizes and natural environments.

rescuers-down-under-1990-first-digital-f.text: The Rescuers Down Under (1990) was the first feature film created entirely digitally without a camera, using Pixar/Disney's CAPS (Computer Animation Production System).

ress-definition.text: RESS (Responsive design with Server-Side components) is a hybrid approach combining client-side responsive design with server-side adaptation; Google recommends pure responsive design over RESS for smartphone sites.

reverse-card-sorting-synonymous-tree-tes.text: Reverse card sorting is synonymous with tree testing and isolates structure from visual design by having participants navigate an existing hierarchy to complete tasks

ribbon-originally-meant-toolbar-pre-1996.text: The term 'ribbon' originally meant toolbar (1988 ESPRIT conference, 1996 Oxford Dictionary of Computing); it now refers to a tabbed multi-toolbar interface — a distinct, more complex element.

ronald-mace-coined-universal-design.text: Architect Ronald Mace coined the term 'universal design'.

rwd-coined-by-marcotte-2010.text: The term 'responsive web design' was coined by Ethan Marcotte in a May 2010 A List Apart article.

rwd-three-core-techniques.text: Responsive web design uses three core techniques: fluid proportion-based grids (relative units like percentages), flexible images (max-width: 100%), and CSS3 media queries.

screen-reader-accessibility-shared-respo.text: Applications that do not comply with accessibility APIs remain inaccessible regardless of screen reader quality — accessibility is a shared responsibility between assistive technology and application developers.

screen-reader-term-origin-ibm-1984.text: The term 'screen reader' originated from IBM's 1984 product 'IBM Screen Reader,' developed by Jim Thatcher and Jesse Wright from an earlier prototype called SAID (~1978).

screen-reader-two-gui-techniques.text: Two core techniques for GUI screen reading are off-screen models (intercept OS draw messages to build internal text representation) and accessibility APIs (query structured representations directly).

scrollbar-agency-reduction-validates-men.text: The scrollbar's progressive agency reduction (paging → interactive scrolling → passive output indicator) is consistent with mental model theory's principle of truth operating at the artifact level: if users represent only the current behavior of an interface element as its complete behavior, then each generation may have difficulty conceiving that scrollbars once offered greater interactive control — the historical alternative would be unlikely to arise as a counterexample. This suggests that truth bias may operate not just within a single interface state but across evolutionary transitions, though direct empirical evidence for this cross-generational effect remains to be established.

justifications.label: Each generation's mental model represents only the current scrollbar behavior as true, confirming truth bias across artifact evolution

scrollbar-bravo-1974-first-scrollbar-int.text: The first scrollbar-like interaction appeared in Bravo (1974) using cursor position and colored mouse buttons.

scrollbar-evolution-interactive-to-passi.text: Scrollbar design evolved over several decades from interactive input controls (Bravo 1974, proportional thumb in Smalltalk 1977, repositioned in Xerox Star 1981-82) to passive output indicators (iPhone 2007), a trajectory consistent with the broader shift from mouse-driven to touch-driven interaction paradigms.

justifications.label: Four dated milestones trace a continuous arc from input to output affordance

scrollbar-gem-1985-first-modern-proporti.text: GEM (1985) produced the first scrollbar with a proportional thumb essentially identical to modern scrollbar behavior.

scrollbar-iphone-2007-output-only-scroll.text: The iPhone (2007) introduced output-only scrollbars that are visible but not directly interactive by the user.

scrollbar-natural-scrolling-macosx-lion-.text: Apple introduced natural scrolling (content moves in same direction as finger movement) in Mac OS X 10.7 Lion (2011), which also removed arrow buttons from scrollbars.

scrollbar-passivity-acceptable-for-mobil.text: The evolution of scrollbars from interactive controls to passive output indicators is acceptable for the mobile-dominant web, where touch gestures replace scroll-track interaction.

justifications.label: Passive scrollbars suit touch interaction — unless 77% of users not scrolling indicates that invisible/passive scrollbars fail to communicate content extent

scrollbar-passivity-validates-enforcemen.text: The scrollbar's 50-year evolution from interactive input control to passive output indicator — a significant behavioral transformation of a persistent web interaction primitive — occurred as part of broader interaction paradigm shifts (mouse to touch) without apparent resistance from the web's technical quality enforcement mechanisms, illustrating how the cognitive-shaping dimension of web platform evolution operates outside the visibility of standards and market enforcement infrastructure.

justifications.label: cross-branch proof — the scrollbar evolution branch and the enforcement blind spot branch share no ancestry but the scrollbar's unresisted behavioral transformation is precisely what the blind spot predicts

scrollbar-proportional-thumb-smalltalk-1.text: Smalltalk (1977) introduced the first proportional scrollbar, where thumb size reflects the ratio of visible content to total content.

scrollbar-triple-demonstration-of-ethica.text: The scrollbar serves as the single most informationally dense artifact in the web's design history: it simultaneously demonstrates the cause of the ethical gap (self-undermining through success — a PARC primitive degraded by the platform its own success created), the perpetuation mechanism (bilateral cognitive invisibility — its 50-year agency reduction invisible to both enforcement and users), and the structural relationship between the two (the same artifact enacts both, proving they are not merely correlated but co-instantiated in the same interaction primitive).

justifications.label: One artifact demonstrates cause (self-undermining) and perpetuation (bilateral invisibility) of the ethical gap — co-instantiation, not correlation

scrollbar-windows-drag-reset-100px.text: On Windows, dragging the scrollbar thumb and moving the pointer approximately 100 pixels away from the thumb resets scroll position to its prior value.

scrollbar-windows-proportional-thumb-add.text: Windows did not support proportional scrollbar thumbs until Windows 95, despite the concept existing since Smalltalk (1977).

scrollbar-xerox-star-moved-to-right-side.text: The Xerox Star (1981-82) moved the scrollbar from the left to the right side of the window.

scrolling-eye-tracking-no-speed-differen.text: Eye-tracking-based auto-scrolling (Sharmin et al., 2013) showed no statistically significant difference in reading speed or performance compared to manual scrolling.

scrolling-hardware-vs-software-distincti.text: Hardware scrolling offsets the displayed image without modifying the frame buffer, while software scrolling requires CPU-driven frame buffer manipulation each frame.

scrolling-inertial-origin-star7-1991.text: Inertial scrolling (content continues moving after touch release with deceleration) was first implemented on Sun Microsystems' Star7 PDA around 1991-1992, not on the iPhone.

scrolling-namco-galaxian-1979-sprite-sys.text: The Namco Galaxian arcade board (1979) pioneered the sprite-over-scrolling-background system that became the basis for NES hardware design.

scrolling-paging-predates-scrolling.text: Paging (full-screen content replacement) predates scrolling as a display navigation technique and requires fewer computational resources.

scrolling-parallax-first-moon-patrol.text: Parallax scrolling (multiple layers scrolling at different rates for pseudo-3D depth) was first featured in the arcade game Moon Patrol.

search-box-classified-data-input-output.text: A search box is classified as a data input-output graphical control element, in the same category as checkboxes, sliders, text boxes, and combo boxes.

search-box-realtime-not-recommended-smal.text: Real-time search result updating (incremental search) is not recommended for small or medium websites due to performance concerns including slow loading, unresponsiveness, and potential browser crashes.

search-box-websocket-240k-rps-benchmark.text: A single WebSocket server instance has been benchmarked handling 240,000 autocomplete requests per second from 1 million concurrent users at approximately 12ms round-trip latency.

section-508-us-federal-it-accessibility.text: Section 508 is a US amendment to the Rehabilitation Act requiring accessible federal information technology.

selective-undo-three-requirements.text: Selective undo has three requirements: undo any action in the history, redo any undone action, and no command is auto-discarded without user request.

self-repair-extends-if-cognitive-shaping.text: The web's self-repair mechanisms could extend beyond their current triple constraint to address the ethical gap — since the accessibility precedent demonstrates that technically specifiable dimensions achieve reliable self-healing, and the presentation tier's three-tier concentration makes the gap architecturally locatable — provided cognitive shaping becomes formally specifiable and detectable by enforcement mechanisms.

justifications.label: The accessibility pipeline proves specifiability enables self-healing; if cognitive shaping became specifiable (the unless goes OUT), the triple constraint would relax for the ethical dimension

self-repair-triply-constrained.text: The web's capacity for self-repair is constrained by three independently derived mechanisms: domain-restricted (self-healing operates only in technically specifiable dimensions like accessibility), scope-confined (self-correction applies only to inherited pre-web dimensions), and orientation-confined (enforcement looks backward at existing quality rather than forward at emerging gaps) — addressing the ethical dimension would require overcoming all three constraints simultaneously, since the ethical dimension is non-specifiable, non-inherited, and forward-looking.

justifications.label: Domain restriction (d11) and double confinement (d8) are independently derived constraints that compound — the ethical dimension fails all three tests

self-undermining-and-ethical-gap-structu.text: The mechanism of self-undermining through success and the web's ethical gap share notable structural parallels: self-undermining operates at both institutional (Xerox PARC originating then losing the GUI) and disciplinary (HCI/UX building then being displaced by their own platforms) levels, producing frozen design knowledge; the ethical gap it contributes to operates through cognitive-shaping mechanisms at micro (UI patterns defeating themselves through habituation) and macro (self-correction confined to inherited dimensions) scales. This suggests that cause and effect may share a similar recursive topology — the process that fossilizes design knowledge produces an ethical gap that itself exhibits scale-invariant properties — though the precise degree of structural isomorphism between the two remains a characterization rather than a demonstrated formal equivalence.

justifications.label: Cause (self-undermining) and effect (ethical gap) both fractal across organizational levels — structural isomorphism, not coincidence

self-undermining-as-general-mechanism-of.text: Self-undermining through success operates as a general mechanism of design knowledge fossilization at both the institutional and discipline levels: Xerox PARC originated foundational interaction primitives but lost control as they were commercialized by others, and HCI/UX disciplines built the platforms and professions whose success rendered the disciplines themselves redundant — in both cases, the knowledge survived as frozen inheritance (platform features, embedded standards) while the living capacity to extend or revise that knowledge was destroyed by the very success it produced.

justifications.label: institutional self-undermining (Xerox PARC) parallels discipline self-undermining (HCI/UX) → success-driven fossilization is the general pattern

self-undermining-escalated-from-institut.text: The self-undermining pattern — previously identified at institutional level (Xerox PARC originated foundational primitives then lost control as they were commercialized) and discipline level (HCI's theory-to-artifact loop built platforms whose success rendered the discipline itself redundant) — may also be operating at the platform level: the web platform's success contributed to mobile dominance, which appears to be undermining aspects of the web platform's quality infrastructure across multiple dimensions (desktop-calibrated standards, interaction models, and enforcement mechanisms tied to the document model). However, the antecedents establish the triple crisis and the self-undermining mechanism separately — the causal claim that mobile dominance is the primary driver of all three quality dimensions degrading simultaneously, rather than a contributing factor among others, goes beyond what the evidence directly supports.

justifications.label: Self-undermining through success has escalated through three levels — institution, discipline, platform — each time affecting a larger scope

self-undermining-fractal-from-artifact-t.text: Self-undermining through success operates fractally across every organizational scale of the web ecosystem: the confirmation dialog demonstrates it at artifact level (safety mechanism → overuse → habituation → self-defeat), HCI and Xerox PARC demonstrate it at institutional/discipline level (creating the desktop platform whose mobile succession made its originators obsolete), and the web platform demonstrates it at ecosystem level (success that displaced the paradigm its quality measures assume) — the pattern's fractal recurrence at the micro scale of individual UI patterns confirms it is a structural property of designed systems, not merely an institutional or disciplinary accident.

justifications.label: Self-undermining is confirmed as fractal by its appearance at the smallest scale (individual UI pattern), not just institution and discipline

self-undermining-generates-persistence-i.text: The web's persistence-immunity decoupling appears to be a product of the self-undermining mechanism: self-undermining contributed to both the conditions for knowledge persistence (platform embedding as a byproduct of disciplinary success) and immunity failure (discipline displacement as a consequence of that same success). Because self-undermining and the ethical gap share fractal topology — repeating at institutional, disciplinary, and platform levels — the same process that preserved design knowledge undermined the capacity to defend it. This structural isomorphism between cause and effect suggests the paradox is not accidental but reflects a recurring pattern inherent in the self-undermining dynamic.

justifications.label: Self-undermining/gap isomorphism (d14) + persistence/immunity decoupling (d13) share a common generative mechanism — the paradox is a necessary structural consequence, not a contingent coincidence

selwyn-goldsmith-curb-cut-designing-for-.text: Selwyn Goldsmith (UK) pioneered the dropped curb/curb cut and authored 'Designing for the Disabled' (1963).

semantic-html-controls-anchor-accessibil.text: The semantic exclusivity taxonomy of native HTML controls (radio=exactly-one, checkbox=zero-or-more, slider=continuous-range) directly implements ARIA Rule 1 — properly used native semantics ARE the foundation of the accessibility stack, not a separate concern.

justifications.label: Input control semantics and accessibility layering converge: correct native HTML is both usability and accessibility

semantic-vs-geometric-zoom.text: Geometric zoom scales objects proportionally; semantic zoom changes an object's representation based on scale level (e.g., a calendar showing years vs. individual days).

server-side-pagination-large-datasets.text: Server-side pagination is preferred for large data sets due to faster initial load, no JavaScript requirement, and support for complex business logic; client-side is appropriate only for very few records.

service-virtualization-over-wire-mocks.text: Service virtualization provides 'over-the-wire test doubles' for SOA and microservices architectures, functioning as the network-level equivalent of mock objects.

seven-principles-universal-design-nc-sta.text: The seven principles of universal design (equitable use, flexibility in use, simple and intuitive, perceptible information, tolerance for error, low physical effort, size and space for approach and use) originated at the Center for Universal Design at North Carolina State University.

shneiderman-8-golden-rules.text: Shneiderman's 8 Golden Rules of interface design: consistency, shortcuts for frequent users, informative feedback, dialog closure, simple error handling, easy reversal, internal locus of control, reduce short-term memory load.

shneiderman-flowchart-research-no-benefi.text: Shneiderman's 1970s experiments showed that detailed flowcharts provided no statistically significant benefit for writing, understanding, or modifying programs — they are a redundant presentation of information already in code.

si-kilogram-prototype-retired-2019.text: The last SI prototype (the kilogram) was retired on May 20, 2019, replaced by a definition based on the Planck constant.

simon-chase-1973-introduced-chunk-term.text: Simon and Chase (1973) introduced the term 'chunk' for memory organization units

single-loop-vs-double-loop-learning.text: Single-loop learning changes decisions within fixed mental models, while double-loop learning revises the mental models themselves.

skeletal-models-preferred-realtime-gestu.text: Skeletal models are preferred for real-time gesture recognition because they use fewer parameters (joint angles + segment lengths) than volumetric models, which require intensive computation of complex 3D surfaces.

sketchpad-first-graphical-cad-1963.text: Sketchpad by Ivan Sutherland (1963) was the first graphical CAD program, operated with a light pen.

skeuomorph-apple-ios7-flat-design-transi.text: Apple shifted from skeuomorphic to flat design starting with iOS 7 at WWDC 2013, led by Jonathan Ive after Scott Forstall's departure.

skeuomorph-differs-from-path-dependence.text: Skeuomorphism preserves visual/ornamental cues from an original medium, while path dependence preserves functional behavior when original reasons no longer apply.

skeuomorph-don-norman-affordances-theory.text: Don Norman connects skeuomorphism to perceived affordances and cultural constraints; his book The Design of Everyday Things is the primary reference.

skeuomorph-etymology-greek-1890.text: The term skeuomorph derives from Greek skeuos (container/tool) + morphe (shape) and has been in use since 1890.

skeuomorph-floppy-disk-save-icon.text: The floppy disk save icon is a skeuomorph that evolved from direct representation to indirect symbol — users recognize its meaning long after the original object became obsolete.

skeuomorph-greek-doric-temples-example.text: Greek Doric order stone temples are a classic skeuomorphic example: triglyphs reproduce carved wooden beam-ends and guttae reproduce wooden pegs, both structurally unnecessary in stone.

slider-classified-data-input-output.text: Sliders are classified under the data input-output category of graphical control elements, alongside checkboxes, spinners, and combo boxes.

slider-combined-with-progress-bar-stream.text: In streaming media (e.g., YouTube), sliders are combined with progress bars — a colored shaded area shows buffered content vs. current playback position.

slider-selects-single-value-from-defined.text: A slider (track bar) is a GUI control element for selecting a single value from a defined range by moving an indicator along a track.

slider-vs-scrollbar-distinction.text: A slider adjusts a discrete value without changing display format, whereas a scrollbar navigates content — this is the key distinction between the two controls.

socialization-commitment-positive-role-c.text: Socialization tactics are positively associated with organizational commitment but negatively correlated with role clarity (Jones 1986; Allen & Meyer 1990) — a counterintuitive finding.

socog-case-2000-first-web-accessibility-.text: The SOCOG case (2000, Australia) was the first successful web accessibility lawsuit under disability discrimination law.

sole-survivor-lacks-ethical-content.text: The web's ethical gap persists through a structural irony: the sole surviving design artifact (progressive disclosure) occupies the enforcement blind spot where ethical intervention must occur, but progressive disclosure addresses cognitive complexity rather than ethical design — the only survivor has the right structural position but the wrong content for the gap it could reach.

justifications.label: position-content mismatch — PD is in the right place (cognitive-shaping dimension) but carries the wrong cargo (complexity management, not ethical constraint)

souders-80-percent-frontend-rule.text: At least 80% of page load time is determined by front-end structure, not back-end (Souders, 2007).

spa-browser-history-pushstate-replacesta.text: SPAs break the browser back/forward button by default; the HTML5 History API (pushState/replaceState) or hash fragment identifiers are used to restore navigation behavior.

spa-can-run-locally-file-uri.text: SPAs can run entirely locally using the file:// URI scheme with browser-based Web Storage for persistence, requiring no server connectivity.

spa-google-hashbang-crawling-deprecated-.text: Google's hash-bang (#!) AJAX crawling scheme for SPAs was introduced in 2009 and deprecated in 2015, replaced by recommendations for SSR, static rendering, or hydration.

spa-no-full-page-reload.text: A single-page application (SPA) dynamically rewrites the current page via JavaScript DOM updates rather than performing full page reloads from the server.

spa-svelte-compiles-no-virtual-dom.text: Svelte compiles components to efficient JavaScript DOM manipulations at build time, shipping no virtual DOM and no framework runtime bundle to the client.

spa-thick-stateless-better-horizontal-sc.text: Thick stateless server architecture scales horizontally better than thick stateful because it maintains no per-client session state requiring sharing or server affinity.

spectral-rainbow-poor-for-sequential-dat.text: Spectral (rainbow) color schemes are poor for sequential data because hues don't naturally convey 'more' or 'less'.

speed-race-1974-early-vertical-scrolling.text: Taito's Speed Race (1974) is cited as an early example of vertical scrolling in video games.

speedindex-measures-visible-area-render-.text: SpeedIndex (measured via WebPageTest) represents the average time for the visible portion of a web page to be displayed.

split-complementary-150-210-degrees.text: Split-complementary color scheme uses a base color plus two colors at 150° and 210° from it.

sql-pagination-limit-offset.text: Database pagination in SQL uses LIMIT/OFFSET to return a subset of rows per query (e.g., SELECT * FROM table LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20), critical in stateless web architectures.

squint-test-validates-hierarchy.text: The squint test reveals visual hierarchy by removing detail; it validates all hierarchy factors except some aspects of character.

static-vs-dynamic-layout-distinction.text: Static layouts provide fixed positioning and precise aesthetic control; dynamic layouts support reflowable content, responsive adaptation, and separate presentation from content.

story-mapping-jeff-patton.text: Story mapping is a two-dimensional backlog visualization (horizontal = product coverage, vertical = priority) developed by Jeff Patton (2005–2014).

story-points-fibonacci-estimation.text: User stories are estimated using story points, typically from the Fibonacci sequence (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13).

structural-ethical-gap-exploitable-throu.text: The web's structural ethical gap (emerging from the convergence of fractal self-sealing, pre-web quality ceiling, and frozen discipline inheritance) is specifically exploitable through the cognitive mechanisms that mental model theory independently predicts: users represent only what is true in a given interface state and fail to generate counterexamples, and the structural gap ensures no enforcement mechanism interrupts this exploitation — the gap provides the opening, the cognitive mechanism provides the entry point.

justifications.label: Structural gap analysis and cognitive exploitation theory converge from independent reasoning chains

style-guide-cascading-precedence.text: Style guides follow a cascading precedence model: project style sheet overrides house style, which overrides industry manual, which overrides language orthography — most specific layer takes precedence.

style-guide-three-categories.text: Style guides fall into three categories: comprehensive (general use), discipline-specific (academic, medical, legal, journalistic), and house/corporate (created by a specific organization).

subtractive-primaries-cmy-not-ryb.text: The true subtractive primaries are CMY (cyan, magenta, yellow), not RYB; red and blue are subtractive secondaries.

successful-intervention-self-defeats-thr.text: Any external intervention that succeeds in closing the web's ethical gap reproduces the very self-undermining dynamic that created it: successful governance creates platform stability, platform stability makes governance appear unnecessary, and apparent unnecessity leads to governance withdrawal — because the mechanism that created the gap (self-undermining through success) and the gap itself are structurally isomorphic, the intervention is self-defeating by structural necessity rather than contingent failure.

justifications.label: Isomorphism between gap and mechanism means any fix inherits the self-undermining property — success is the precondition for its own withdrawal

This isn't a gap that linking can fill — the premises actively contradict each other.
